label: Level 1 spells tier list, [Updated] part 1 (Animal Friendship to Goodberry)

items.verdict: weakest crowd control in the game, and only usable in the easiest encounters
solid for any warlock, game-breaking on an Abjuration Wizard whose Arcane Ward preserves the temp HP
too little damage, scales badly, and forces a squishy warlock into the middle of enemies
never worth a slot early; good late against bosses immune to stronger control, since few resist it
d4 to attacks and saves for 10 turns; the spell beats the Whispering Promise ring on duration
weak damage on a bad save; only Light Domain clerics, who get it free, will cast it
unreliable and low impact in combat, and cantrips already cover the dialogue use
damage plus a chosen surface with no concentration; ice surfaces are near-stuns and it bypasses immunities
HP-capped so it fails against dangerous enemies, and Fog Cloud blinds without that limit
concentration-free turn denial that upcasts to multiple enemies; every higher-level slot competes with it
BUGGED — the forced-attack effect is not implemented when you cast it, so it only grants disadvantage
applies wet for doubled cold and lightning damage, and saves scarce water bottles in Honour mode
healing numbers never keep up; saved only by Star Druid chalice triggers and free Life Cleric access
free ritual; dodges crimes, gains race dialogue and prices, and unlocks race-locked items and shapeshift gear
concentration-free damage plus two turns of Frightened on a WIS save; effectively stuns melee enemies
loses to just using the slot on a smite; only for War Cleric dips stacking radiant riders
free ritual giving the whole party a bonus-action teleport; cannot be upcast, so cast it per character
bonus action on top of a normal attack; Bounty Hunter's disadvantage fixes the STR save
big no-move AoE, but it is flammable and druids get free spider webs from Wild Shape
all-day bonus-action dash, mostly superseded by Enhance Leap; take it for dash and concentration item synergies
huge radius, but other spells grant advantage and do more; outclassed at its own job
seven temp HP for a slot, and it blocks better temp HP sources since they do not stack
free ritual traversal; must be cast before falling in BG3, not as a reaction
free raven that scouts, blinds and soaks a hit; heavy micromanagement, and the Cheeky Quasit competes
no-save blind in a big AoE plus a guaranteed hiding spot; can win fights against immobile enemies
healing potions are more plentiful and heal more; only real use is infinite camp supplies

negated mention for Disguise Self — "it's not quite S tier" — immediately before the A verdict at 40:13
restatement of Divine Favour's C verdict ("this is another C tier spell where...")
conditional bump for Find Familiar — "I can definitely see bumping it up to S tier" if you enjoy heavy summon micromanagement
negated mention for Fog Cloud — "I don't think it quite cracks S tier" — immediately before the A verdict at 1:06:40
